newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola closes lower on new crop CBOT soy slide.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola closes lower on new crop CBOT soy slide.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed lower on spillover weakness from sharp declines in new crop CBOT soybeans with late export-related buying helping to curb losses on the May contract, floor sources said.
However, they noted that nearby old crop canola had failed to match the relatively strong performance of old crop CBOT soybeans with U.S. oilseed supplies tighter than in Canada.
"We've got enough (canola) to carry us through," one WCE oilseed trader said.
May closed off $1.30 at $427.60. The May WCE crush profit margin fell to -17.98 Monday from -14.96 Thursday.

Crushers were small buyers of new crop months but were deterred from chasing the market aggressively by the decline in new crop soybeans on news USDA had forecast U.S. soybean acreage at 68.80 million acres, well above trade forecasts.
Statistics Canada is due to issue its first forecast for Canadian planting intentions on April 30.
Flaxseed prices closed lower but overall performed much more strongly than canola or soybeans, aided by commercial buying in fairly heavy volume, traders said.
"Flax held very well. We have the best volume in a couple of weeks and commercials were buying," one WCE trader said.
Western barley futures ended lower won commission house and commercial selling. May barley ended off $1.50 at $142.40. Wheat was also lower with May down $0.20 at $171.50.
December feed peas ended up US$1.50 at US$191.50. Oats were tradeless.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
